text: Up next Published on 22 April 2026 Author Michael Kozlowski Tags remarkable , remarkable tablet , staff Remarkable, the company that makes distraction-free e-notebooks that can be used for editing PDF files, freehand drawing, or taking notes. They have announced that they are downsizing, that over 200 staff members will lose their jobs, and that the CEO will also be replaced.  It has only been eight months since the previous downsizing, when the number of employees was reduced from 580 to 500. At the same time, American Philip Hess will step down as CEO after two years. He will be replaced by Vegard Gullaksen Veiteberg, who previously led the company on an interim basis. Remarkable has struggled with declining demand over the past year, while prices for key components such as memory chips have skyrocketed amid the growing artificial intelligence industry. The company has resorted to i ncreasing the prices of its Paper tablets , such as the Remarkable 2 and Remarkable Paper Pro, as well as some accessories. Chairman Marius Juul Mølle told a local newspaper that “There is a tougher macro picture and global unrest. We have noticed weaker demand and thus falling sales.” The Remarkable now faces strong competition from Amazon’s Kindle Scribe, which outsells it by a significant margin.
